newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends flat after lower U.S. CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends flat after lower U.S. CPI data.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended virtually flat on Tuesday around C$1.3860 (US$0.7215) in active trading after the U.S. reported lower than expected consumer prices data, dealers said. * The U.S. May CPI rose 0.1 percent, off economists' forecasts for a rise of 0.2 percent, but on target for CPI ex-food and energy at 0.2 percent.
"I think from a numbers point of view everything fit in to what I think we already knew," Farrill said.
Traders said recent data indicated a U.S. economy moving along at a reasonable pace with little inflationary pressure.
They said that meant there was little evidence to cause the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next monetary policy meeting at the start of July.
The Federal Open Market Committee will meet to discuss interest rates and inflation July 1-2.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar climbed to 81.67 yen from Monday's 81.63 yen close, but fell to 1.2476 marks from Monday's 1.2487 marks.
New Canadian provincial and corporate debt issues

On the crosses, the Canadian dollar A stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation number, however, may not be enough to push the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its next Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1-2.

"We'll wait and see what the U.S. numbers bring us," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy. "Given the fact that last week's numbers were on the soft side, I don't think the market is expecting any major change."
"Any inflationary numbers would probably surprise the market," Farrill said.
